This violent, fast moving and destructive tornado, which became the first EF5 tornado of the outbreak touched down near the city of [Philadelphia, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia,_Mississippi "Philadelphia, Mississippi"), on April 27. The tornado touched down at 2:30 p.m. CDT (19:30 UTC) and traveled for nearly 29 miles (47 km) through [Neshoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neshoba_County,_Mississippi "Neshoba County, Mississippi"), [Kemper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kemper_County,_Mississippi "Kemper County, Mississippi"), [Winston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_County,_Mississippi "Winston County, Mississippi"), and [Noxubee Counties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noxubee_County,_Mississippi "Noxubee County, Mississippi"), reaching a maximum width of a 1⁄2-mile (0.80 km).[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-93)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Philadelphia,_MS_EF5_Survey-94) The tornado killed three people, injured eight others, and caused $1.1 million in damage across its path.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Philadelphia,_MS_EF5_Survey-94)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-95)

The supercell thunderstorm that produced this tornado formed around 1:00 p.m. CDT south of [Jackson, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson,_Mississippi "Jackson, Mississippi").[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-PhiladelphiaEF5_1-96) Traveling briskly to the northeast, it warranted a severe thunderstorm warning within 25 minutes and was deemed potentially tornadic by 1:36 p.m. CDT.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-PhiladelphiaEF5_1-96)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-97) A tornado finally touched down at 2:30 p.m. CDT just east of the [Philadelphia Municipal Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Municipal_Airport "Philadelphia Municipal Airport"). It quickly intensified and began producing EF5 damage by 2:38 p.m. CDT; extreme ground scouring, up to 2 feet (0.61 m) deep in places, occurred in northeastern Neshoba County. After crossing into Kemper County, the tornado obliterated a mobile home, killing all three inside.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Philadelphia,_MS_EF5_Survey-94) It reached EF5 strength a second time near the Kemper–Winston county line where extreme ground scouring again took place and pavement was scoured.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Philadelphia,_MS_EF5_Survey-94)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-PhiladelphiaEF5_1-96) Extreme tree damage took place along the track and it ultimately dissipated at 3:00 p.m. CDT about 6 miles (9.7 km) north of [Mashulaville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mashulaville,_Mississippi "Mashulaville, Mississippi").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Philadelphia,_MS_EF5_Survey-94)

This was the first tornado to cause F5/EF5 damage in [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi "Mississippi") since the [Candlestick Park tornado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_Candlestick_Park_tornado_outbreak#Candlestick_Park_tornado "1966 Candlestick Park tornado outbreak") on March 3, 1966. Additionally, the formation of the [Smithville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smithville,_Mississippi "Smithville, Mississippi") tornado later that day marked the first time since statistics have been kept that two EF5 tornadoes have been recorded in Mississippi on the same day. Prior to this, the last confirmed EF5 tornado was the [Parkersburg, Iowa tornado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Parkersburg%E2%80%93New_Hartford_tornado "2008 Parkersburg–New Hartford tornado") on May 25, 2008.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Philadelphia,_MS_EF5_Survey-94)

### Cullman/Arab, Alabama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Cullman/Arab, Alabama")]

Cullman/Arab, Alabama[![Image 375: Damaged building in the aftermath of a tornado, with debris scattered around](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Cullman_Alabama_First_Methodist_Church_Damage.jpg/330px-Cullman_Alabama_First_Methodist_Church_Damage.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cullman_Alabama_First_Methodist_Church_Damage.jpg)
The First Methodist Church was damaged by the tornado.
Meteorological history
Formed April 27, 2011, 2:40 p.m. [CDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Daylight_Time "Central Daylight Time") ([UTC−05:00](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%E2%88%9205:00 "UTC−05:00"))
Dissipated April 27, 2011, 3:38 p.m. CDT (UTC−05:00)
Duration 58 minutes
EF4 tornado
_on the [Enhanced Fujita scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced\_Fujita\_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale")_
Highest winds 190 mph (310 km/h)
Overall effects
Casualties 6 fatalities, 48+ injuries

Rated as a high-end EF4, this highly visible multiple-vortex tornado tracked directly through downtown Cullman.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Long_Track_Tornado_Hits_Cullman,_Alabama-98) The tornado touched down at 2:40 p.m. CDT (19:40 UTC) on April 27 and tracked a 47-mile (76 km) damage path through [Cullman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cullman_County,_Alabama "Cullman County, Alabama"), [Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_County,_Alabama "Morgan County, Alabama"), and [Marshall Counties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_County,_Alabama "Marshall County, Alabama"), causing six deaths.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-April_27,_2011,_Cullman,_Alabama_EF4_Tornado-49) The Cullman tornado first touched down on the north side of [Lewis Smith Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Smith_Lake "Lewis Smith Lake") and caused light structural damage near [Crane Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crane_Hill,_Alabama "Crane Hill, Alabama") before intensifying and tracking directly towards Cullman, snapping numerous trees and heavily damaging several homes. The tornado entered Cullman while being tracked and broadcast live via several tower cameras, including those operated by Birmingham [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company") affiliate [WBRC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WBRC "WBRC") (channel 6) and [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") affiliate [WBMA-LD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WBMA-LD "WBMA-LD")/[WCFT-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WSES "WSES")/[WJSU-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WGWW "WGWW") (channels 58, 33, and 40 - "_ABC 33/40_"), for several minutes.In all, a total of 867 residences and 94 businesses within the city of Cullman were damaged or destroyed.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Long_Track_Tornado_Hits_Cullman,_Alabama-98)

[![Image 376: Aftermath of a tornado, showing a concrete foundation surrounded by debris and damaged structures](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/High-end_EF4_damage_to_a_home_northwest_of_Arab%2C_Alabama.jpg/250px-High-end_EF4_damage_to_a_home_northwest_of_Arab%2C_Alabama.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:High-end_EF4_damage_to_a_home_northwest_of_Arab,_Alabama.jpg)

High-end EF4 damage to a home northwest of Arab, where five fatalities occurred.

The tornado then passed just north of [Fairview](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairview,_Alabama "Fairview, Alabama") at EF4 intensity, completely destroying homes and debarking numerous hardwood trees. Pieces of debris were found speared through vehicles in this area.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-April_27,_2011,_Cullman,_Alabama_EF4_Tornado-49) In [Ruth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth,_Alabama "Ruth, Alabama"), just north of [Arab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab,_Alabama "Arab, Alabama"), a large but poorly anchored brick home was swept completely away in this area, with the debris scattered 100 yards (91 m) from the foundation. Arab's power grid was completely crippled by the tornado's effects, and many roads in the area were obstructed by downed trees and power lines. The tornado damaged and destroyed several other homes, garages, and sheds north of [Union Grove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Grove,_Alabama "Union Grove, Alabama") before it crossed the [Tennessee River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_River "Tennessee River") just downstream of [Guntersville Dam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guntersville_Dam "Guntersville Dam"). It snapped numerous trees in a forested area before dissipating southeast of [New Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hope,_Alabama "New Hope, Alabama").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-April_27,_2011,_Cullman,_Alabama_EF4_Tornado-49)

Widespread power outages occurred in the immediate aftermath of the tornado, which were largely centered in Cullman County.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Almost 200 power poles in and around Cullman were leveled, and 4,000 volunteers from the [Tennessee Valley Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Valley_Authority "Tennessee Valley Authority") helped to restore power, although some residents were still without power a week after the tornado.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-99) The State of Alabama gave $5,989,728 (2011 [USD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USD "USD")) to the City of Cullman to aid with recovery efforts, and a further $1,294,892 (2011 USD) to Cullman County.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:4-100) A plan was also set in place by the [University of Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Alabama "University of Alabama") to help fund recovery efforts.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-101) Six people were killed by the tornado; five in Ruth and one in rural Cullman County.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-102) The five deaths in Ruth occurred when the tornado directly impacted a well-constructed home at EF4 intensity, leveling the building and killing all of the residents of the home; all were in the same family. The sixth death as a result of the tornado took place in Cullman County, in the tornado's early stages.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:1-103)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104)[Storm chaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storm_chasing "Storm chasing") Dan Whittaker, who was observing the tornado as it moved through Cullman near him, stated that "this is not like any tornado I've seen anywhere."[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-105)

### Hackleburg–Phil Campbell–Tanner–Harvest, Alabama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Hackleburg–Phil Campbell–Tanner–Harvest, Alabama")]

Hackleburg–Phil Campbell–Tanner–Harvest, Alabama[![Image 377: Satellite view showing the path of the Hackleburg-Phil Campbell tornado in Alabama, 2011](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Hackleburg-Phil_Campbell_tornado_scar.png/330px-Hackleburg-Phil_Campbell_tornado_scar.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hackleburg-Phil_Campbell_tornado_scar.png)
The scar of the tornado.
Meteorological history
Formed April 27, 2011, 3:05 p.m. [CDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Daylight_Time "Central Daylight Time") ([UTC−05:00](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%E2%88%9205:00 "UTC−05:00"))
Dissipated April 27, 2011, 4:50 p.m. CDT (UTC−05:00)
Duration 1 hour, 45 minutes
EF5 tornado
_on the [Enhanced Fujita scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced\_Fujita\_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale")_
Highest winds 210 mph (340 km/h)
Overall effects
Casualties 71 fatalities, 145+ injuries

This devastating, long-tracked and violent EF5 wedge tornado was the deadliest of the outbreak. It first touched down in [Marion County, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_County,_Alabama "Marion County, Alabama"), about 5 miles (8.0 km) west-southwest of [Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamilton,_Alabama "Hamilton, Alabama") around 3:00 p.m. CDT (21:00 UTC) on April 27, leaving massive damage along its track. The storm would eventually reach the [Hackleburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hackleburg,_Alabama "Hackleburg, Alabama") area, completely leveling many homes and businesses, including a large [Wrangler, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrangler_(Jeans) "Wrangler (Jeans)") factory. Most of the structures in downtown Hackleburg were badly damaged and Hackleburg High School was destroyed. Well-built homes were wiped cleanly from their foundations, extensive wind-rowing of debris occurred, trees were completely debarked, and cars were thrown hundreds of yards. According to the [American Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Red_Cross "American Red Cross"), 75 percent of the town was destroyed.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-106) While initially rated as an EF3, the rating was increased to EF5 after further analysis of the damage, making it the first F5/EF5 tornado in Alabama since the [Birmingham tornado of April 8, 1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_1998_Birmingham_tornado "April 1998 Birmingham tornado").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Marion_survey-107)

[![Image 378: Weather radar map displaying a severe storm with areas of high intensity rainfall, indicating potentially hazardous weather conditions](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/22/2011_Hackleburg-Phil_Campbell_tornado_radar_KGWX_2011-04-27_2033Z.png/250px-2011_Hackleburg-Phil_Campbell_tornado_radar_KGWX_2011-04-27_2033Z.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2011_Hackleburg-Phil_Campbell_tornado_radar_KGWX_2011-04-27_2033Z.png)

Radar image of the tornado as it neared the town of [Phil Campbell, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Campbell,_Alabama "Phil Campbell, Alabama"), with a [debris ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debris_ball "Debris ball") evident

Soon after crossing into [Franklin County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_County,_Alabama "Franklin County, Alabama"), the town of [Phil Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Campbell,_Alabama "Phil Campbell, Alabama") experienced significant devastation of the same magnitude as Hackleburg. Numerous homes, some of which were well-constructed, were swept away as the tornado tore through town. At least three churches along the path sustained significant damage, with one church in the town being completely destroyed and having only the foundation slab remaining. Mobile homes throughout the path were completely destroyed, and their mangled frames were tossed at least 25 to 50 yards (23 to 46 m). Cars were tossed and destroyed throughout the path of the tornado, with one car wrapped around a debarked tree. A 25-foot (7.6 m) section of pavement was torn from a road in this area as well. The most intense damage along the path occurred northeast of Phil Campbell in the rural community of Oak Grove, where vehicles were carried long distances and mangled beyond recognition, large trees were completely debarked, and large brick homes with extensive anchoring were obliterated with the debris wind-rowed hundreds of yards away. The tornado continued into [Lawrence County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_County,_Alabama "Lawrence County, Alabama"), impacting the [Mount Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Hope,_Lawrence_County,_Alabama "Mount Hope, Lawrence County, Alabama") community, where significant devastation was incurred to single-family homes and a restaurant. Nothing but the foundation and a pile of debris remained at the restaurant site, and a small portion of the restaurant's foundation slab buckled.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Huntsville_EF5-108)

[![Image 379: Extensive damage from a natural disaster, with debris scattered across the landscape and two cars visible among the wreckage](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Toney2011.jpg/250px-Toney2011.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Toney2011.jpg)

A destroyed neighborhood in Toney, Alabama.

The tornado moved northeast, producing EF3 damage in and around [Langtown](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Langtown,_Alabama&action=edit&redlink=1 "Langtown, Alabama (page does not exist)"). The tornado re-intensified to EF4 strength as it passed near [Moulton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moulton,_Alabama "Moulton, Alabama") and [Trinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity,_Alabama "Trinity, Alabama"), debarking trees, mangling, and leveling homes. It then continued through the northwest corner of [Morgan County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_County,_Alabama "Morgan County, Alabama"), crossed Wheeler Lake, and moved into [Limestone County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone_County,_Alabama "Limestone County, Alabama"), coming within 2 miles (3.2 km) of [Browns Ferry Nuclear Power Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Browns_Ferry_Nuclear_Power_Plant "Browns Ferry Nuclear Power Plant"). The tornado caused power outages in the area, and the plant had to be shut down. The tornado continued towards the small community of Tanner.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWS-HUN-SWS-04282141-109)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-TFP-nuke-110)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-HUN-132.1mi-111)[Tanner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanner,_Alabama "Tanner, Alabama") experienced a large swath of EF4 damage and a narrow corridor of "high-end EF4 to near-EF5 damage". The storm "completely wiped clean" several well constructed homes with anchor bolting.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWS-HUN-SWS-04282141-109) As the storm crossed [US 72](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_72 "U.S. Route 72") in eastern Limestone County, the tornado destroyed a [Doppler radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doppler_weather_radar "Doppler weather radar") operated by Huntsville [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") affiliate [WAFF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WAFF_(TV) "WAFF (TV)") (channel 48) and continued into East Limestone, a heavily populated area of Limestone County where homes in subdivisions were damaged or destroyed at high-end EF3 strength. As the storm crossed into Madison County, it approached the densely populated suburban communities of [Harvest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvest,_Alabama "Harvest, Alabama") and [Toney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toney,_Alabama "Toney, Alabama"), where it either damaged or destroyed hundreds of homes, especially in the Anderson Hills and Carter's Gin subdivisions. Many homes were reduced to rubble, and the damage in this area was rated mainly EF3 with a small pocket of EF4 damage in Harvest. The tornado completely destroyed a [Piggly Wiggly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piggly_Wiggly "Piggly Wiggly") grocery store in Harvest and severely damaged a convenience store and local bank, which was shut down for months following the event.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-SWDJW-04272011ToneyHarvestDestruction-112) The storm progressed across Pulaski Pike in northwest Madison County, damaging many homes, and dissipated soon afterwards. In all, hundreds of homes received moderate to major damage along the path from Limestone to Madison County with many of these being total losses.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWS-HUN-SWS-04282141-109)

Initially, the tornado was thought to have continued into [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee"). However, updates to the [Damage Assessment Toolkit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damage_Assessment_Toolkit "Damage Assessment Toolkit") (DAT) and analysis by damage surveyors, including a 2022 re-analysis of the outbreak by the [National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Oceanic_and_Atmospheric_Administration "National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration") (NOAA) and [National Severe Storms Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Severe_Storms_Laboratory "National Severe Storms Laboratory") (NSSL), determined that the Hackleburg tornado lifted after Madison County and assessed the portion in Tennessee to be a separate EF3 tornado.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Damage_Viewer-113)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-2022Analysis-114)

In total, this tornado killed 71 people, all in Alabama.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-spc_fatal-3) This made it the deadliest single tornado ever to strike the state of Alabama as well as (at the time) the deadliest in the United States since the 1955 [Udall, Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udall,_Kansas "Udall, Kansas"), tornado that killed 80 people.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-115)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-116) In addition to being the deadliest, this tornado also had one of the longest tracks of any tornado in the outbreak, with its path extending 102 miles (164 km) across Northern Alabama.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-2022Analysis-114)

In response to the damage in Phil Campbell, one of the hardest hit communities, writer [Phil Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Campbell_(writer) "Phil Campbell (writer)") organized a fundraising and relief effort composed of 20 people with the name Phil Campbell or variations thereof. They traveled to the community from places as far away as Australia to aid in the cleanup effort. Many of these people had planned to attend a convention in June 2011 to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the city's incorporation.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-117)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-118)

### Reform–Oakman–Cordova–Blountsville, Alabama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Reform–Oakman–Cordova–Blountsville, Alabama")]

Reform–Oakman–Cordova–Blountsville, Alabama[![Image 380: A tornado hovers in the sky behind a red barn](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/ae/2011_Central_Alabama_Tornado_at_EF4_intensity.webp/330px-2011_Central_Alabama_Tornado_at_EF4_intensity.webp.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2011_Central_Alabama_Tornado_at_EF4_intensity.webp)
The tornado at peak intensity moving over rural areas.
Meteorological history
Formed April 27, 2011, 3:40 p.m. [CDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Daylight_Time "Central Daylight Time") ([UTC−05:00](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%E2%88%9205:00 "UTC−05:00"))
Dissipated April 27, 2011, 5:56 p.m. CDT (UTC−05:00)
Duration 2 hours, 16 minutes
EF4 tornado
_on the [Enhanced Fujita scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced\_Fujita\_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale")_
Highest winds 170–180 mph (270–290 km/h)[[note 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Higher_Winds-120)
Overall effects
Casualties 13 fatalities, 54+ injuries

This violent and extremely long-tracked EF4 tornado touched down at 3:40 p.m. CDT (20:40 UTC) in northeastern [Pickens County, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickens_County,_Alabama "Pickens County, Alabama"), where it strengthened while impacting structures at EF0 and EF1 intensity, moving past several smaller towns.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Cordova_tornado-119) As the tornado moved into [Cordova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cordova,_Alabama "Cordova, Alabama") it reached EF3 intensity and heavily damaged the town. The tornado continued to strengthen as it moved across Alabama, reaching EF4 intensity as it passed northwest of [Sumiton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumiton,_Alabama "Sumiton, Alabama"). The tornado retained this intensity as it caused sporadic damage across rural Alabama, destroying numerous homes and debarking trees. It dissipated south of [Red Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Hill,_Alabama "Red Hill, Alabama"), lifted south-southwest of [Guntersville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guntersville,_Alabama "Guntersville, Alabama") at 5:56 p.m. CDT (22:56 UTC). Thousands of trees were downed along the tornado's path.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Marshall_County_survey-121) This tornado was on the ground for two hours and sixteen minutes, tracking for 127.8 miles (205.7 km) across seven counties making it the longest track tornado of the outbreak. It was rated as a low-end EF4 with winds of 170 mph (270 km/h). In total, 13 people were killed and 54 others were injured.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Cordova_tornado-119)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Marshall_County_survey-121)

Cordova was devastated by the tornado, which was the second major tornado to hit the community on April 27.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-122)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-123) Several businesses and other buildings were destroyed or heavily damaged in and outside of the town, and four were killed in the downtown area.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The city of Cordova was awarded $5,098,515 equivalent to $7,127,000 in 2024 to aid with recovery efforts after the tornado; Blount County was awarded $758,572 (equivalent to $1,060,000 in 2024).[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:4-100) Recovery efforts continued for months after the tornadoes.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-124) In the weeks and months after the tornado, numerous fires started in downtown Cordova within the rubble, which further damaged structures and temporarily stunted recovery efforts.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-125)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-126)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-127)

### Smithville, Mississippi/Shottsville, Alabama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Smithville, Mississippi/Shottsville, Alabama")]

Smithville, Mississippi/Shottsville, Alabama[![Image 381: An outdoor scene shows a tornado touching down, with trees and land visible in the foreground](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/d/d5/2011_smithville_tornado.png/330px-2011_smithville_tornado.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2011_smithville_tornado.png)
The tornado at maximum intensity while impacting the east side of Smithville.
Meteorological history
Formed April 27, 2011, 3:42 p.m. [CDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Daylight_Time "Central Daylight Time") ([UTC−05:00](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%E2%88%9205:00 "UTC−05:00"))
Dissipated April 27, 2011, 4:23 p.m. CDT (UTC−05:00)
Duration 41 minutes
EF5 tornado
_on the [Enhanced Fujita scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced\_Fujita\_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale")_
Highest winds 205 mph (330 km/h)
Overall effects
Casualties 23 fatalities, 137 injuries

This extraordinarily violent and fast moving EF5 wedge tornado, with estimated winds of up to 205 mph (330 km/h), struck the town of [Smithville, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smithville,_Mississippi "Smithville, Mississippi"), at 3:47 p.m. CDT (20:47 UTC) on April 27, resulting in catastrophic damage and numerous fatalities.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSMemphisSmithvilleEF5-128) The tornado began 3 miles (4.8 km) west-southwest of Smithville along the [Tennessee–Tombigbee Waterway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee%E2%80%93Tombigbee_Waterway "Tennessee–Tombigbee Waterway") near the [Glover Wilkins Lock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glover_Wilkins_Lock "Glover Wilkins Lock") at 3:42 p.m. CDT (20:42 UTC), snapping numerous trees near the Smithville Recreation Area. The tornado then rapidly intensified as it approached town, reaching EF5 intensity. As the storm crossed Davis Road South, the ground was deeply scoured in a nearby field.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Smith._Damage_Imagery-129) The tornado swept away numerous homes and structures as it moved northeast, following [Highway 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_Highway_25 "Mississippi Highway 25"). A semi-truck was thrown a considerable distance and destroyed in this area, and at one residence that was swept away, part of the concrete foundation slab was pulled up and dislodged slightly.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSMemphisSmithvilleEF5-128)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Smith._Damage_Imagery-129) Multiple well-anchored brick homes were completely swept away, and a large brick funeral home was reduced to a bare slab as the tornado exited at the northeast side of town, with the debris scattered and wind-rowed into an adjacent wooded area. Nearby granite tombstones were blown over in the opposite direction of the tornado's passage. Overall, the tornado destroyed 117 structures in Smithville and damaged 50 others, killing 16 people.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Smithville_NCDC-130) The tornado weakened as it continued through rural areas northeast of town and moved into [Itawamba County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itawamba_County,_Mississippi "Itawamba County, Mississippi"), where it downed numerous trees and power lines and caused roof damage to a house before exiting the county.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Smith._Damage_Imagery-129)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-131)

[![Image 382: Two images showing weather radar with greens and blues to the left and yellows and reds to the right](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/Smithville_Tornado_Radar.png/250px-Smithville_Tornado_Radar.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Smithville_Tornado_Radar.png)

Radar image showing the supercell and [hook echo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hook_echo "Hook echo") of the storm that produced the Smithville tornado.

The tornado continued across the [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama "Alabama") state line into [Marion County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_County,_Alabama "Marion County, Alabama"), where it caused EF1-strength damage near [Bexar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bexar,_Alabama "Bexar, Alabama"). Continuing northeast, the tornado re-intensified as it struck the rural community of [Shottsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shottsville,_Alabama "Shottsville, Alabama") at high-end EF3 intensity, where homes and mobile homes were destroyed and seven people were killed, and it produced additional high-end EF3 damage as it continued north of [Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamilton,_Alabama "Hamilton, Alabama").[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-auto-132) More structures were impacted as the tornado approached and crossed into [Franklin County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_County,_Alabama "Franklin County, Alabama"). The tornado then dissipated near the town of [Hodges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hodges,_Alabama "Hodges, Alabama") at 4:23 p.m. CDT (21:23 UTC). The damage path was 37.3 miles (60.0 km) long and 3⁄4 mile (1.2 km) wide at its widest point, and it killed a total of 23 people along its path. 137 other people were injured.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-auto-132)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-133)

### Pisgah–Flat Rock–Higdon, Alabama/Trenton, Georgia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Pisgah–Flat Rock–Higdon, Alabama/Trenton, Georgia")]

Pisgah–Flat Rock–Higdon, Alabama/Trenton, Georgia[![Image 383: An aerial view showing houses and buildings with blue tarps covering the roofs](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Aerial_of_Trenton%2C_Georgia_following_an_EF4_tornado_on_April_27%2C_2011.png/330px-Aerial_of_Trenton%2C_Georgia_following_an_EF4_tornado_on_April_27%2C_2011.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aerial_of_Trenton,_Georgia_following_an_EF4_tornado_on_April_27,_2011.png)
An aerial view of the damage in Trenton, Georgia by the tornado.
Meteorological history
Formed April 27, 2011, 4:01 p.m. [CDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Daylight_Time "Central Daylight Time") ([UTC−05:00](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%E2%88%9205:00 "UTC−05:00"))
Dissipated April 27, 2011, 4:57 p.m. CDT (UTC−05:00)
Duration 56 minutes
EF4 tornado
_on the [Enhanced Fujita scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced\_Fujita\_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale")_
Highest winds 190 mph (310 km/h)
Overall effects

This multiple-vortex EF4 tornado that originated from the Cullman supercell, with maximum sustained winds of up to 190 mph (310 km/h), devastated portions of [Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_County,_Alabama "Jackson County, Alabama") and [DeKalb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeKalb_County,_Alabama "DeKalb County, Alabama") counties in Alabama, as well as [Dade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dade_County,_Georgia "Dade County, Georgia") and [Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walker_County,_Georgia "Walker County, Georgia") counties in Georgia along a 47-mile-long (76 km) path at times up to 1,260 yards (1,150 m) wide, killing 14 people and injuring at least 50 others.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NOAA-134)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Storm_Events_Database-135)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-ncdc.noaa.gov-136)

The tornado touched down north of [Section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Section,_Alabama "Section, Alabama"), initially producing EF0 to EF1 tree damage. The tornado rapidly intensified to low-end EF4 strength as it passed northwest of [Pisgah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pisgah,_Alabama "Pisgah, Alabama") and [Rosalie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosalie,_Alabama "Rosalie, Alabama"), destroying numerous mobile homes and block foundation homes, scattering the debris hundreds of yards and killing three people. Thousands of trees were snapped and debarked, vehicles were thrown up to 50 yards (46 m) in different directions, and barns and chicken houses were heavily damaged, along with the roof of a church.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NOAA-134) As it passed near [Flat Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flat_Rock,_Alabama "Flat Rock, Alabama") and [Higdon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higdon,_Alabama "Higdon, Alabama"), the tornado reached high-end EF4 strength, mowing down thousands of trees in this rural area. The tornado later crossed into Georgia and crossed [Interstate 59](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_59 "Interstate 59") as it struck [Trenton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trenton,_Georgia "Trenton, Georgia") at EF3 intensity, killing two people. Dozens of homes in Trenton were either completely destroyed or sustained major damage, and tens of thousands of trees were downed in the area. A grocery store, two apartment complexes, and a funeral home were destroyed as well.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Storm_Events_Database-135)

The tornado weakened to EF2 strength as it struck [Flintstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flintstone,_Georgia "Flintstone, Georgia") further to the northeast, but still resulted in major damage. Numerous trees and power lines were downed, 7 homes were destroyed, 26 sustained major damage, and 35 sustained minor damage in the Flintstone area. The tornado continued northeast, weakening to EF0 strength before finally dissipating near [Fort Oglethorpe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Oglethorpe,_Georgia "Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia").[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-ncdc.noaa.gov-136)

### Tuscaloosa–Birmingham, Alabama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Tuscaloosa–Birmingham, Alabama")]

Tuscaloosa–Birmingham, Alabama[![Image 384: Aerial view of a destroyed building complex and debris scattered around](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Tuscaloosa_Apartment_Complex.JPG/330px-Tuscaloosa_Apartment_Complex.JPG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tuscaloosa_Apartment_Complex.JPG)
The Tuscaloosa apartment complex was destroyed by the tornado.
Meteorological history
Formed April 27, 2011, 4:43 p.m. [CDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Daylight_Time "Central Daylight Time") ([UTC−05:00](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%E2%88%9205:00 "UTC−05:00"))
Dissipated April 27, 2011, 6:14 p.m. CDT (UTC−05:00)
Duration 1 hour, 31 minutes
EF4 tornado
_on the [Enhanced Fujita scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced\_Fujita\_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale")_
Highest winds 190 mph (310 km/h)
Overall effects
Casualties 64 fatalities, ~1,500 injuries

This large and catastrophic multiple-vortex [wedge tornado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wedge_tornado "Wedge tornado") touched down in rural [Greene County, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greene_County,_Alabama "Greene County, Alabama"), and tracked across neighboring [Tuscaloosa County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuscaloosa_County,_Alabama "Tuscaloosa County, Alabama"), including the southern and eastern portions of [Tuscaloosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuscaloosa,_Alabama "Tuscaloosa, Alabama") at around 5:10 p.m. CDT (22:10 UTC) on April 27.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-massive-50)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSBir.Tusc.Survey-137) Debris from the tornado was reported to be falling from the sky across [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham,_Alabama "Birmingham, Alabama") over 20 miles (32 km) away in [Jefferson County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_County,_Alabama "Jefferson County, Alabama"). Skycams operated by Tuscaloosa television station [WVUA-CA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WVUA-CD "WVUA-CD") (channel 7) as well as Birmingham [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company") affiliate [WBRC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WBRC "WBRC") (channel 6), [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") affiliate [WBMA-LD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WBMA-LD "WBMA-LD")/[WCFT-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WCFT-TV "WCFT-TV")/[WJSU-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WJSU-TV "WJSU-TV") (channels 58, 33, and 40), and [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") affiliate [WIAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIAT "WIAT") (channel 42) captured live footage of the tornado as it struck Tuscaloosa; WIAT received awards, including a regional [Edward R. Murrow Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_R._Murrow_Award_(Radio_Television_Digital_News_Association) "Edward R. Murrow Award (Radio Television Digital News Association)") for "Outstanding Live Coverage" of the event).[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-138) As the tornado traveled east to 35th Street and Kauloosa Avenue, the Tuscaloosa Environmental Services and [Cintas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cintas "Cintas") facilities suffered severe damage. Numerous homes and apartment buildings in the Rosedale and Forest Lake neighborhoods, as well as a P&P Grocery store in Rosedale, were devastated. Several stores and restaurants in a business district at the intersection of McFarland Boulevard and 15th Street, near the DCH Regional Medical Center, were reduced to rubble. Buildings on 35th Street, between [Interstate 359](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_359 "Interstate 359") and Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard, were also completely destroyed. The Alberta City neighborhood in eastern Tuscaloosa sustained catastrophic damage as numerous homes, apartment buildings, and a shopping center were completely leveled. Additional low-end EF4 damage occurred in the Tuscaloosa suburb of [Holt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holt,_Alabama "Holt, Alabama") further to the northeast, as several homes were leveled or swept away in that area. The tornado then exited the Tuscaloosa area and moved through dense forest towards Birmingham, downing and debarking thousands of trees at low-end EF3 intensity.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-139)

[![Image 385: Doppler weather radar displaying a supercell thunderstorm with high reflectivity and velocity signatures](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/Radar_image_of_the_2011_Tuscaloosa_tornado_April_27%2C_2011_2210Z.png/250px-Radar_image_of_the_2011_Tuscaloosa_tornado_April_27%2C_2011_2210Z.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Radar_image_of_the_2011_Tuscaloosa_tornado_April_27,_2011_2210Z.png)

Radar reflectivity and velocity image of the supercell that produced the tornado at 22:10 UTC (5:12 p.m. CDT) as it struck Tuscaloosa, with a [debris ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debris_ball "Debris ball") clearly visible.

The [University of Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Alabama "University of Alabama") shut down its campus briefly during the course of the storm itself, resuming regular activities within minutes. Upon realizing the extent of the storm damage immediately off-campus, including areas of off-campus student housing, the university shut down all academic and extracurricular activities for the remainder of the day, and then, still later, for the remaining ten days of the academic semester. All final exams were cancelled, with all registered students receiving a final grade based on their grade as of the day of the storm. Spring commencement ceremonies were postponed until August 6.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-140) The university itself was undamaged by the storm, though six students enrolled at the university were later discovered to have perished.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-141)

Many stations, including WIAT, WBMA/WCFT/WJSU, [WTVY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTVY_(TV) "WTVY (TV)") (channel 4) in [Dothan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dothan,_Alabama "Dothan, Alabama") and [WSFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WSFA "WSFA") (channel 12) in [Montgomery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montgomery,_Alabama "Montgomery, Alabama"), showed television cameras capturing the event as the tornado moved east-northeast across the western and northern suburbs of Birmingham around 6:00 p.m. CDT (23:00 UTC). It rapidly intensified to its maximum intensity and grew to its maximum width as it approached the area. Several suburbs in the area were severely damaged by the massive tornado as it tore through the west side of Birmingham, resulting in fatalities. The suburbs of [Concord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concord,_Alabama "Concord, Alabama") and [Pleasant Grove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleasant_Grove,_Alabama "Pleasant Grove, Alabama") were devastated by the high-end EF4 tornado as it moved northeast, flattening entire neighborhoods. The tornado then weakened, but still caused heavy EF2 damage to the community of [McDonald Chapel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald_Chapel,_Alabama "McDonald Chapel, Alabama"). As the tornado entered the Birmingham city limits, it impacted the [Pratt City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pratt_City,_Alabama "Pratt City, Alabama") neighborhood while still at EF2 strength, damaging numerous homes and apartment buildings. The tornado then struck the suburb of [Fultondale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fultondale,_Alabama "Fultondale, Alabama"), causing additional EF2 damage to homes and businesses before rapidly weakening and dissipating north of [Tarrant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarrant,_Alabama "Tarrant, Alabama").[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSBir.Tusc.Survey-137)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-142)

The [National Weather Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Weather_Service "National Weather Service") determined the path length of this violent tornado to be 80.7 miles (129.9 km) with a maximum damage path width of 1.5 miles (2.4 km). The tornado's most intense damage indicated peak winds of around 190 mph (310 km/h); therefore, it was given a final rating of EF4. Reports from Tuscaloosa indicated 44 people were killed, with an additional 20 deaths in Birmingham.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSBir.Tusc.Survey-137)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-143) Overall this tornado killed 64 people and injured more than 1500.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-spc_fatal-3)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSBir.Tusc.Survey-137)[President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")[Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") and [First Lady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_the_United_States "First Lady of the United States")[Michelle Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Obama "Michelle Obama") visited Tuscaloosa on April 29, taking a ground tour of some of the affected areas. Obama was quoted as saying that he had "never seen devastation like this". He stated further that he had already declared a federal state of emergency in Alabama.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-nprttown-144)

### Fackler–Stevenson–Bridgeport, Alabama/Haletown, Tennessee

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Fackler–Stevenson–Bridgeport, Alabama/Haletown, Tennessee")]

Fackler–Stevenson–Bridgeport, Alabama/Haletown, Tennessee[![Image 386: Tornado appears to head toward a cluster of structures in a grassy area](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/0/08/2011_Bridgeport_EF4_tornado.jpg/330px-2011_Bridgeport_EF4_tornado.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2011_Bridgeport_EF4_tornado.jpg)
The tornado as it moved through Bridgeport.
Meteorological history
Formed April 27, 2011, 5:05 p.m. [CDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Daylight_Time "Central Daylight Time") ([UTC−05:00](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%E2%88%9205:00 "UTC−05:00"))
Dissipated April 27, 2011, 5:31 p.m. CDT (UTC−05:00)
Duration 26 minutes
EF4 tornado
_on the [Enhanced Fujita scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced\_Fujita\_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale")_
Highest winds 180 mph (290 km/h)
Overall effects
Casualties 1 fatality

This EF4 tornado, with winds of up to 180 mph (290 km/h), touched down in the community of [Fackler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fackler,_Alabama "Fackler, Alabama") at 5:05 p.m. CDT (22:05 UTC) on April 27, initially causing minor damage to mobile homes and downing trees. The tornado then moved northeast toward [Stevenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevenson,_Alabama "Stevenson, Alabama"), where large trees were downed, several roofs were damaged, a trailer was tipped over, and a shed was partially destroyed. It then reached EF3 intensity, and 24 metal high-tension truss towers were twisted and flattened northeast of [Stevenson Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevenson_Airport "Stevenson Airport"). In this area, a mobile home was obliterated and a site-built house was collapsed. Two other homes sustained structural damage, two mobile homes were rolled on their side, and a metal barn was destroyed as well. The tornado then continued to the northeast and reached EF4 strength, with the most significant damage being located near the intersection of County Roads 255 and 256. Here, a home was reduced to its foundation, a concrete slab at the front of the home was pulled up, and a set of concrete stairs was ripped from the foundation. A compact car was thrown about 50 yards (46 m) as well.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Fackler_tornado-145)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-FacklerNCDC-146)

Continuing, the tornado reduced two more well-built and well-anchored homes to their block foundations and threw another car approximately 50 yards (46 m). Several large trees were snapped off just above the ground, a third home was left with no walls standing, and a mobile home was completely demolished and strewn along County Road 256 as well. The tornado continued northeastward, destroying a cinder block garage and damaging a mobile home along 6th Street, just southeast of the city of [Bridgeport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgeport,_Alabama "Bridgeport, Alabama"). It then crossed the [Tennessee River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_River "Tennessee River"), producing significant tree damage as it passed a couple miles to the northwest of [Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryant,_Alabama "Bryant, Alabama") before moving into [Marion County, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_County,_Tennessee "Marion County, Tennessee").[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Fackler_tornado-145)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-FacklerNCDC-146) The tornado entered [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee") along Lakeview Drive near [Moore Crossing](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moore_Crossing,_Tennessee&action=edit&redlink=1 "Moore Crossing, Tennessee (page does not exist)") and [Nickajack Dam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickajack_Dam "Nickajack Dam"). It crossed [Highway 156](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_State_Route_156 "Tennessee State Route 156") near the dam and proceeded to cross [Nickajack Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickajack_Lake "Nickajack Lake") three times near [Interstate 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_24 "Interstate 24") at EF2 strength, downing numerous trees before dissipating in a bend of the Tennessee River northeast of [Haletown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haletown,_Tennessee "Haletown, Tennessee") at 5:31 p.m. CDT (22:31 UTC).

The tornado travelled 30.24 miles (48.67 km) through Jackson and Marion Counties and had a peak width of 1,320 yards (1,210 m). One person was killed by the tornado in Jackson County, a teenager near Bridgeport.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Fackler_tornado-145)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-FacklerNCDC-146)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-147)

### Sawyerville–Eoline, Alabama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Sawyerville–Eoline, Alabama")]

Sawyerville–Eoline, Alabama[![Image 387: House completely demolished by a tornado, its components scattered on the lawn](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/EF3_damage_to_a_brick_home_near_Sawyerville%2C_Alabama.jpg/330px-EF3_damage_to_a_brick_home_near_Sawyerville%2C_Alabama.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:EF3_damage_to_a_brick_home_near_Sawyerville,_Alabama.jpg)
Low-end EF3 damage to a brick home northeast of Sawyerville, Alabama.
Meteorological history
Formed April 27, 2011, 5:30 p.m. [CDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Daylight_Time "Central Daylight Time") ([UTC−05:00](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%E2%88%9205:00 "UTC−05:00"))
Dissipated April 27, 2011, 6:55 p.m. CDT (UTC−05:00)
Duration 1 hour, 25 minutes
EF3 tornado
_on the [Enhanced Fujita scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced\_Fujita\_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale")_
Highest winds 145 mph (233 km/h)
Overall effects

This strong and long-tracked EF3 wedge tornado touched down in extreme southwest [Greene County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greene_County,_Alabama "Greene County, Alabama") to the west-southwest of [Tishabee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tishabee,_Alabama "Tishabee, Alabama"), near the [Sumter County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumter_County,_Alabama "Sumter County, Alabama") border, at 5:30 p.m. CDT (22:30 UTC) and moved northeast. After having touched down in a rural area on the east side of the [Tombigbee River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tombigbee_River "Tombigbee River"), the tornado quickly intensified to high-end EF2 strength along County Road 69. Moving northeast, the tornado damaged a barn and destroyed two small churches and at least four mobile homes. Two people sustained minor injuries in Greene County as the tornado continued along a primarily rural path northeast, moving across the [Black Warrior River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Warrior_River "Black Warrior River") and into [Hale County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hale_County,_Alabama "Hale County, Alabama").[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Sawyerville/Eoline_tornado-148)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-GreeneCo_NCDC-149)

Leaving behind six fatalities and forty more injuries, the tornado maintained its intensity as it moved into the [Talladega National Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talladega_National_Forest "Talladega National Forest"). It downed a significant number of trees before moving into [Bibb County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bibb_County,_Alabama "Bibb County, Alabama") north of [Alabama State Highway 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_State_Route_25 "Alabama State Route 25").[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Sawyerville/Eoline_tornado-148)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-HaleCoEF3_NCDC-150) In Bibb County, the tornado continued moving northeastward through the Talladega National Forest at EF3 intensity, with thousands more trees being knocked down and partially debarked. Almost immediately after exiting the national forest, the tornado directly impacted the small community of [Eoline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eoline,_Alabama "Eoline, Alabama") along [U.S. Highway 82](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_82 "U.S. Route 82"), northwest of [Brent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brent,_Alabama "Brent, Alabama") and [Centerville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centerville,_Alabama "Centerville, Alabama"). Around one dozen mobile homes and single-family site-built homes were destroyed.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Sawyerville/Eoline_tornado-148)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BibbCoEF3_NCDC-151)

Northeast of Eoline, the tornado weakened to EF2 intensity, continuing to cause significant damage as it crossed County Road 9, [Alabama State Highway 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_State_Route_5 "Alabama State Route 5"), and County Road 26, south of [West Blocton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Blocton,_Alabama "West Blocton, Alabama"). Several mobile homes and site-built homes were either destroyed or sustained major damage. Along the path, thousands of trees were downed. The tornado continued to weaken as it moved to the east of West Blocton, continuing to knock down trees. More trees were downed as the tornado crossed the [Cahaba River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cahaba_River "Cahaba River") and lifted just northeast of [Marvel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel,_Alabama "Marvel, Alabama") at 6:55 p.m. CDT (23:55 UTC), not far from the [Shelby County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shelby_County,_Alabama "Shelby County, Alabama") border.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Sawyerville/Eoline_tornado-148)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BibbCoEF3_NCDC-151)

The tornado was rated as an EF3, with maximum sustained winds of 145 mph (233 km/h). It remained on the ground for almost an hour and a half, traversing 72.13 miles (116.08 km), being, at times, about one mile (1.6 km) wide. In total, seven people were killed and at least 52 others were injured.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Sawyerville/Eoline_tornado-148)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-GreeneCo_NCDC-149)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-HaleCoEF3_NCDC-150)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BibbCoEF3_NCDC-151)

### Raleigh–Rose Hill–Enterprise, Mississippi/Yantley–Uniontown, Alabama

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Raleigh–Rose Hill–Enterprise, Mississippi/Yantley–Uniontown, Alabama")]

Raleigh–Rose Hill–Enterprise, Mississippi/Yantley–Uniontown, Alabama[![Image 388: A small tornado is visible in the distance over a field, with trees and bushes in the foreground](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Smith_Jasper_Clarke_Counties_tornado_2011-04-27.jpg/330px-Smith_Jasper_Clarke_Counties_tornado_2011-04-27.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Smith_Jasper_Clarke_Counties_tornado_2011-04-27.jpg)
The EF4 Enterprise tornado, as it was in southeast Mississippi.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Raleigh,_MS_tornado-152)
Meteorological history
Formed April 27, 2011, 5:42 p.m. [CDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Daylight_Time "Central Daylight Time") ([UTC−05:00](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%E2%88%9205:00 "UTC−05:00"))
Dissipated April 27, 2011, 8:35 p.m. CDT (UTC−05:00)
Duration 2 hours, 53 minutes
EF4 tornado
_on the [Enhanced Fujita scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced\_Fujita\_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale")_

Overall effects
