This extremely long-tracked and violent EF4 tornado touched down near [Raleigh, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raleigh,_Mississippi "Raleigh, Mississippi"), in [Smith County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smith_County,_Mississippi "Smith County, Mississippi") at 5:42 p.m. CDT (22:42 UTC), and continued into the [Uniontown, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniontown,_Alabama "Uniontown, Alabama"), area before dissipating. The tornado initially downed trees, blew skirting from mobile homes, and tore shingles from roofs. The tornado intensified as it moved northeast across Smith County and produced up to EF2 and EF3 damage. One mobile home was picked up, bounced a couple times, and thrown into a tree line, where it was torn apart and debris was scattered up to a mile away, including the frame. The tornado mowed down a stand of pine trees and destroyed two frame houses, with major damage to the interior walls, and the exterior walls completely destroyed. Many power poles were snapped, a mobile home was annihilated, and a large shop building was completely destroyed as well. It then moved into [Jasper County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasper_County,_Mississippi "Jasper County, Mississippi") and snapped and debarked many pine trees. The first area of EF4 damage was observed near [Louin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louin,_Mississippi "Louin, Mississippi") as a frame home and several mobile homes were completely destroyed, with parts of the mobile homes being thrown long distances, and some of the frame home foundation being swept clean. The tornado caused significant damage to a poultry farm and cattle ranch before it weakened briefly. It then destroyed two mobile homes and caused extensive tree and power line damage. The tornado then produced a relatively narrow path of EF1-strength tree and power line damage for several miles, until re-intensifying near to EF3 strength near [Rose Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Hill,_Jasper_County,_Mississippi "Rose Hill, Jasper County, Mississippi").[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Raleigh,_MS_tornado-152)

Southeast of Rose Hill, the tornado removed most of the roof of a frame home and caused heavy damage to the exterior walls, took a large section of roof off another frame home, completely destroyed a large mobile home, and caused extensive tree damage. The tornado then weakened again and entered [Clarke County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarke_County,_Mississippi "Clarke County, Mississippi") as an EF0 while only downing a few trees. The tornado strengthened again and downed trees and power lines as it crossed [Interstate 59](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_59 "Interstate 59"). Several other homes and mobile homes were destroyed as the tornado moved along the south side of [Enterprise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enterprise,_Clarke_County,_Mississippi "Enterprise, Clarke County, Mississippi"). At the same time, [Sean Casey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Casey_(filmmaker) "Sean Casey (filmmaker)") of Team TIV shot the tornado with his new 3D camera as it was crossing I-59, making this the first tornado ever shot in 3D. Another area of EF4 damage was observed east of Enterprise as a new home undergoing completion was leveled, with the debris swept off the foundation. Many more frame homes were heavily damaged nearby. Many mobile homes were destroyed and trees were downed in this area as well. It then weakened slightly to EF3 strength and produced heavy damage to more houses and mobile homes near [Snell](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Snell,_Mississippi&action=edit&redlink=1 "Snell, Mississippi (page does not exist)") and [Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy,_Mississippi "Energy, Mississippi"). It also downed many more trees and power lines before moving into [Choctaw County, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choctaw_County,_Alabama "Choctaw County, Alabama"), southwest of [Yantley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yantley,_Alabama "Yantley, Alabama"). The tornado killed seven people and injured fourteen others on its 65-mile (105 km) portion of the path that was in [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi "Mississippi").[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Raleigh,_MS_tornado-152)

[![Image 389: The image shows a damaged landscape with broken trees and debris after a natural disaster, possibly a tornado or hurricane, with the sun setting in the background](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/EF4_damage_to_a_home_near_Enterprise%2C_Mississippi.png/250px-EF4_damage_to_a_home_near_Enterprise%2C_Mississippi.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:EF4_damage_to_a_home_near_Enterprise,_Mississippi.png)

Low-end EF4 damage to a home near Enterprise, Mississippi.

In Choctaw County, the tornado traveled 27.5 miles (44.3 km) as it caused extensive damage to homes (one of which was destroyed at EF3 strength), and numerous other structures. Several mobile homes were destroyed and many trees were either snapped or completely uprooted. The tornado then moved into [Sumter County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumter_County,_Alabama "Sumter County, Alabama").[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Yantley_survey-153) In Sumter County, the tornado caused significant damage to homes and mobile homes before it crossed the [Tombigbee River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tombigbee_River "Tombigbee River") and moved into [Marengo County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marengo_County,_Alabama "Marengo County, Alabama"). It continued causing significant tree damage as well as destroying several homes and outbuildings along a 26.7-mile (43.0 km) path in this county. The tornado then entered [Perry County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perry_County,_Alabama "Perry County, Alabama"), the final portion of the path, where it damaged two outbuildings and a grain silo as well as causing significant tree damage before lifting just north of [Uniontown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniontown,_Alabama "Uniontown, Alabama") at 8:35 p.m. CDT (01:35 UTC). The damage in Sumter, Marengo, and Perry Counties was rated EF2.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Uniontown_tornado-154)

This tornado was on the ground for nearly three hours, having traveled 122.04 miles (196.40 km) across seven counties in two states. Seven people were killed and another 17 were injured.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Raleigh,_MS_tornado-152)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Yantley_survey-153)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Uniontown_tornado-154)

### Fyffe–Rainsville–Sylvania, Alabama/Rising Fawn, Georgia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Fyffe–Rainsville–Sylvania, Alabama/Rising Fawn, Georgia")]

Fyffe–Rainsville–Sylvania, Alabama/Rising Fawn, Georgia[![Image 390: Tornado funnel cloud looming over a green landscape](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f0/Rainsville_Tornado_Dana_Dobbins.png/330px-Rainsville_Tornado_Dana_Dobbins.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rainsville_Tornado_Dana_Dobbins.png)
The Rainsville tornado exiting town at EF5 strength.
Meteorological history
Formed April 27, 2011, 6:19 p.m. [CDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Daylight_Time "Central Daylight Time") ([UTC−05:00](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%E2%88%9205:00 "UTC−05:00"))
Dissipated April 27, 2011, 6:55 p.m. CDT (UTC−05:00)
Duration 36 minutes
EF5 tornado
_on the [Enhanced Fujita scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced\_Fujita\_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale")_
Highest winds>200 mph (320 km/h)
Overall effects
Casualties 25 fatalities, unknown injuries

This violent and devastating multiple-vortex tornado that originated from the Cordova supercell was rated as an EF5, making it so far the most recent tornado to be rated at that intensity in Alabama. It began in the [Lakeview](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakeview,_Alabama "Lakeview, Alabama") community northeast of [Geraldine, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geraldine,_Alabama "Geraldine, Alabama"), at 6:19 p.m. CDT (23:19 UTC), during the late afternoon of April 27. The tornado tracked northeastward for 36.63 miles (58.95 km) generally parallel to and just east of [Highway 75](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_State_Route_75 "Alabama State Route 75") through [Fyffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fyffe,_Alabama "Fyffe, Alabama"), [Rainsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainsville,_Alabama "Rainsville, Alabama"), and [Sylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvania,_Alabama "Sylvania, Alabama") and into [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)"), killing 25 people.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Rainsville,_AL_Tornado_Survey-155)

Initial damage in Lakeview consisted of structural damage to small buildings and snapped trees. The tornado grew in intensity as it struck Fyffe, where more significant damage occurred. Past Fyffe, the tornado became violent, and its width increased from around 50 yards (46 m) to 0.5 miles (800 m) as it entered eastern Rainsville, reaching EF5 intensity as it destroyed numerous homes and businesses. A [Huddle House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huddle_House "Huddle House") restaurant, the Rainsville Civic Center, and a credit union were destroyed. Vehicles were also thrown, including a school bus that was completely stripped down to its chassis.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-156) Numerous homes in the Rainsville area were swept completely away, with debris strewn up to a mile from the foundations. Some of these homes were connected to their foundations with anchor bolts and foundation straps. Trees were debarked and mobile homes were completely destroyed as well.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Rainsville,_AL_Tornado_Survey-155) Damage was particularly intense just northeast of Rainsville, and one well-built stone house in this area was completely obliterated, with the debris strewn well away from the structure. A large supporting cement and stone pillar was ripped completely out of the ground at this residence, pulling up a section of concrete foundation in the process. Scouring and pock-marking of the ground was noted in this area. Numerous homes were swept away along Lingerfelt Road as well. At one house that was swept away in this area, supporting concrete anchors were ripped out of the ground, a concrete porch was ripped off with pieces strewn up to 150 yards (140 m) away, a pick-up truck from the home was found mangled in pieces over 250 yards (230 m) away, and a safe weighing 800 pounds (360 kg) was pulled off its anchorage and thrown into a wooded area 600 feet (180 m) away. When found, the safe's door had been ripped open and completely off.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Rainsville,_AL_Tornado_Survey-155) An underground storm shelter in this area had much of its dirt covering scoured away, the occupants of which reported that structure heaved upwards slightly as the tornado passed overhead. Pavement was scoured from several roads in the area, and a concrete porch was torn away and broken in half at another residence that was swept away.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-157)

[![Image 391: Pile of rubble and debris on a patch of land, with a grassy field and some trees in the background](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/EF5_damage_to_a_home_along_Skaggs_Rd.jpg/250px-EF5_damage_to_a_home_along_Skaggs_Rd.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:EF5_damage_to_a_home_along_Skaggs_Rd.jpg)

An obliterated home along Skaggs Road.

The tornado continued across the eastern fringes of [Sylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvania,_Alabama "Sylvania, Alabama"), where a church was completely destroyed, a section of sidewalk was pulled up, and additional homes were swept away and scattered, though it was revealed that these homes were pushed off their foundations with limited anchorage. A high-end EF4 rating was applied in this area as a result.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Rainsville,_AL_Tornado_Survey-155) The tornado continued to level additional homes as it passed near [Henagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henagar,_Alabama "Henagar, Alabama") and [Ider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ider,_Alabama "Ider, Alabama"), at which point it began to closely parallel [Interstate 59](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_59 "Interstate 59"). It crossed into [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)") near [Fox Mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fox_Mountain,_Georgia&action=edit&redlink=1 "Fox Mountain, Georgia (page does not exist)") at EF1 intensity with winds of 110 mph (180 km/h). It tracked three miles (4.8 km) into Georgia, crossing Interstate 59 and moving through [Rising Fawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rising_Fawn,_Georgia "Rising Fawn, Georgia") before lifting outside of the community at 6:55 p.m. CDT/7:55 p.m. EDT (23:55 UTC). Damage in Georgia was limited to trees and power lines and minor structural damage to a few homes. This tornado came from the same supercell that produced the EF4 tornado that hit the town of [Ringgold, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ringgold,_Georgia "Ringgold, Georgia"), about 30 minutes later.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Rainsville,_AL_Tornado_Survey-155)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-158)

### Shoal Creek Valley–Ohatchee–Piedmont, Alabama/Cave Spring, Georgia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Shoal Creek Valley–Ohatchee–Piedmont, Alabama/Cave Spring, Georgia")]

Shoal Creek Valley–Ohatchee–Piedmont, Alabama/Cave Spring, Georgia[![Image 392: Tornado over a lake, framed by silhouetted trees](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Shoal_Creek_Valley_Alabama_Tornado_April_27%2C_2011.jpg/330px-Shoal_Creek_Valley_Alabama_Tornado_April_27%2C_2011.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shoal_Creek_Valley_Alabama_Tornado_April_27,_2011.jpg)
The Shoal Creek Valley/Ohatchee EF4 tornado.
Meteorological history
Formed April 27, 2011, 6:28 p.m. [CDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Daylight_Time "Central Daylight Time") ([UTC−05:00](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%E2%88%9205:00 "UTC−05:00"))
Dissipated April 27, 2011, 9:15 p.m. [EDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Daylight_Time "Eastern Daylight Time") (UTC−05:00)
Duration 1 hour, 47 minutes
EF4 tornado
_on the [Enhanced Fujita scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced\_Fujita\_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale")_
Highest winds 180 mph (290 km/h)
Overall effects
Casualties 22 fatalities, 85 injuries

After the Tuscaloosa/Birmingham tornado dissipated, the same supercell produced this EF4 tornado at 6:28 p.m. CDT (23:28 UTC) near [Argo, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argo,_Alabama "Argo, Alabama"), in eastern [Jefferson County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_County,_Alabama "Jefferson County, Alabama"). It went on to devastate the rural community of Shoal Creek Valley, located between [Ashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashville,_Alabama "Ashville, Alabama") and [Ragland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ragland,_Alabama "Ragland, Alabama") in [St. Clair County, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Clair_County,_Alabama "St. Clair County, Alabama").[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Shoal_Creek-Ohatchee_survey-159)

After touching down southwest of Argo, the tornado continued northeast of [Odenville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odenville,_Alabama "Odenville, Alabama"), producing EF0 to EF1 tree damage. Further east, the tornado intensified to EF3 strength and entered the rural community of Shoal Creek Valley, following along County Road 22/Shoal Creek Road for approximately 12.5 miles (20.1 km), with the path and width varying greatly along the road. Many homes were left with only interior walls standing in this area. Some section of this path segment had damage that was much worse on one side of the road than the other, while other areas showed equal devastation on both sides of the road. The tornado reached mid-range EF4 intensity towards the end of the valley as it approached [Neely Henry Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neely_Henry_Lake "Neely Henry Lake"). Additional homes were destroyed in this area, one was swept away, and thousands of trees were mowed down and debarked. The tornado maintained EF4 strength as it crossed the lake and tore across the north edge of [Ohatchee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohatchee,_Alabama "Ohatchee, Alabama"), completely leveling or sweeping away numerous waterfront homes. Damage ranged from downed trees and roof damage to total destruction as the tornado roared through this area at 50–60 mph (80–97 km/h), packing winds of over 180 mph (290 km/h). The official count of homes destroyed or heavily damaged in Shoal Creek Valley and Ohatchee was 256. Most phone lines, power lines and poles were destroyed, and water lines were severed by uprooted trees. Entire homes were leveled, and in some cases completely removed by the storm, leaving only brick steps, a fireplace and chimney, or a slab behind. Barns, vehicles, tractors and heavy farming equipment were shredded and thrown up to 0.5 miles (0.80 km) away from where they originated. Livestock were thrown and killed, and the initial human death toll of 13 would eventually rise to 15 in the area.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Shoal_Creek-Ohatchee_survey-159)

[![Image 393: Area that was severely damaged by a tornado, with the remains of houses and trees scattered around the landscape](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/EF4_damage_to_a_home_in_Shoal_Creek_Valley%2C_Alabama.jpg/250px-EF4_damage_to_a_home_in_Shoal_Creek_Valley%2C_Alabama.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:EF4_damage_to_a_home_in_Shoal_Creek_Valley,_Alabama.jpg)

A home swept off its foundation along Robins Mill Road.

The tornado caused mainly EF3 damage to homes as it passed north of [Wellington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington,_Alabama "Wellington, Alabama"), though a small pocket of EF4 damage occurred in the small rural community of [Webster's Chapel](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Webster%27s_Chapel,_Alabama&action=edit&redlink=1 "Webster's Chapel, Alabama (page does not exist)"), where a church and several homes were completely leveled or swept away, trees were reduced to stumps, and many other homes were left with only interior walls standing.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Shoal_Creek-Ohatchee_survey-159)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Damage_Viewer-113) The Silver Lakes Golf Course also sustained major damage in this area, where at least 50,000 trees were flattened and buildings were damaged or destroyed.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-160) Continuing northeast, the tornado produced high-end EF3 damage north of [Piedmont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piedmont,_Alabama "Piedmont, Alabama"), destroying mobile homes, snapping numerous trees, and leveling a house. Additional homes were leveled at high-end EF3 intensity near [The Indian Mountain Tract](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Indian_Mountain_Tract&action=edit&redlink=1 "The Indian Mountain Tract (page does not exist)") before it continued across rural areas into [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)").[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Shoal_Creek-Ohatchee_survey-159) Many outbuildings and homes were destroyed, and many trees were downed across [Polk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polk_County,_Georgia "Polk County, Georgia"), [Floyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floyd_County,_Georgia "Floyd County, Georgia"), and [Bartow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bartow_County,_Georgia "Bartow County, Georgia") counties. Severe damage was noted near [Cave Spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cave_Spring,_Georgia "Cave Spring, Georgia") where chicken houses and homes were damaged or destroyed, and several people were injured. The damage in Georgia was rated EF2. The tornado finally dissipated near [Kingston, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingston,_Georgia "Kingston, Georgia"), after having travelled for 97.33 miles (156.64 km) over the span of an hour and 47 minutes.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-161)

This tornado's final death toll, combining fatalities in both St. Clair and [Calhoun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calhoun_County,_Alabama "Calhoun County, Alabama") counties in Alabama, would eventually come to 22.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-spc_fatal-3)

### Ringgold, Georgia/Southeast Tennessee

A house completely swept away at EF4 intensity in Ringgold.
Meteorological history

EF4 tornado

Overall effects

From the same supercell that spawned the EF5 tornado that struck Rainsville, this violent multiple-vortex tornado struck portions of extreme northern Georgia and southeast Tennessee during the mid-evening of April 27. It touched down along Davis Ridge Road in [Catoosa County, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catoosa_County,_Georgia "Catoosa County, Georgia"), and moved through the town of [Ringgold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ringgold,_Georgia "Ringgold, Georgia") at EF3 strength, destroying numerous homes and businesses.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSRinggoldEF4-162) A [Baymont Inn & Suites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baymont_Inn_%26_Suites "Baymont Inn & Suites"), located near [Interstate 75](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_75 "Interstate 75") was partially destroyed by the tornado, along with a [McDonald's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald%27s "McDonald's"), a [Taco Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Bell "Taco Bell"), and several gas stations located on Highway 151 in Ringgold at the Interstate 75 interchange (exit 348). The Catoosa County Department of Family and Children Services and other businesses on Nashville Street in downtown Ringgold were also heavily damaged. The Kellerhals Center for Visual Arts Education at Ringgold High School was destroyed (RHS itself had minor damage), and Ringgold Middle School was heavily damaged.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSRinggoldEF4-162)[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-163) Past downtown Ringgold, the tornado reached EF4 intensity as it tore through a subdivision along Cherokee Valley Road at the north edge of town. Twelve homes were completely obliterated and swept away at that location (though they were not well-built). Several trees were denuded and debarked in this area as well. There were 74 destroyed homes and/or businesses, 60 with major damage, and 118 with minor damage for a total of 252 affected structures in the Ringgold area. Eight people were killed, mainly at the subdivision along Cherokee Valley Road.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-164)

[![Image 395: Destruction from a tornado, revealing a collapsed brick building with a car visible inside, surrounded by debris and damaged trees](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Apison%2C_TN_tornado_damage.PNG/250px-Apison%2C_TN_tornado_damage.PNG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apison,_TN_tornado_damage.PNG)

EF4 damage to a large brick home in Apison, Tennessee.

The storm then crossed the Tennessee state line at 8:28 p.m. [EDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") (00:28 UTC), and moved into [Hamilton County, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamilton_County,_Tennessee "Hamilton County, Tennessee"), striking the small town of [Apison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apison,_Tennessee "Apison, Tennessee") at high-end EF4 strength, where large homes were leveled or swept away, 150 others were damaged, and thousands of trees were snapped and uprooted.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSApisonEF4-165)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-166) The tornado then crossed into Bradley County at low-end EF4 strength, moving across the southern and eastern fringes of [Cleveland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland,_Tennessee "Cleveland, Tennessee") and affecting mainly residential areas, though a few businesses were damaged or destroyed as well. Subdivisions in the southern part of the city sustained major damage, with numerous houses destroyed and a few that were leveled.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSApisonEF4-165) Four people were killed in Cleveland, and many others were injured.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSApisonEF4-165)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-167) Several trees were felled in Polk County as the tornado weakened to EF1-strength, before it crossed into McMinn County.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSApisonEF4-165) The tornado re-intensified to EF2 and destroyed two houses and a mobile home before lifting south of [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens,_Tennessee "Athens, Tennessee").[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-168)

The tornado killed 20 people and injured hundreds more along its 48-mile (77 km) path across Catoosa, Hamilton, Bradley, Polk, and McMinn counties. The tornado was given a rating of EF4 with peak wind speed of 190 mph (310 km/h). The damage path of the tornado was 1⁄2 mile (0.80 km) wide. This tornado was only the eighth in Georgia to be categorized as an F4/EF4 on the ([Enhanced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced_Fujita_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale")) [Fujita scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fujita_scale "Fujita scale") since 1950, when current official tornado records begin.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSRinggoldEF4-162)[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSApisonEF4-165)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-EF4-169) It would be the last EF4 tornado in the state until [March 26, 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_March_24%E2%80%9328,_2021#Franklin%E2%80%93Newnan%E2%80%93Peachtree_City,_Georgia "Tornado outbreak sequence of March 24–28, 2021"), when [Newnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newnan,_Georgia "Newnan, Georgia") was struck just after midnight.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-170)

All roads in and out of Ringgold were closed until the morning of April 29; after roads leading to the affected areas were re-opened, residents and business owners were allowed to return, being allowed entry only by providing identification, and informing police a reason why they were entering into the area, in order to curb looting in the storm-damaged areas.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Ringgold-171)

On January 23, 2025, Anthony W. Lyza with the [National Severe Storms Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Severe_Storms_Laboratory "National Severe Storms Laboratory") along with Harold E. Brooks and Makenzie J. Kroca with the [University of Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oklahoma "University of Oklahoma")'s School of Meteorology published a paper to the [American Meteorological Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Meteorological_Society "American Meteorological Society"), where they stated the tornado in Apison was an "EF5 candidate". The paper was of the opinion that the EF5 starting wind speed should be 190 mph (310 km/h) instead of 201 mph (323 km/h).[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Lyza2025-54)

### Eclectic–Lake Martin–Dadeville, Alabama

This long-tracked and violent [tornado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado "Tornado") struck areas around [Lake Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Martin "Lake Martin") in east central Alabama. The tornado caused large swaths of EF4 damage, particularly to homes on the shores of Lake Martin.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-172) Many homes were completely swept off their foundations, and hundreds of trees were uprooted by the tornado. It reached EF3 intensity at least three times, and reached its maximum intensity of low-end EF4 in Lake Martin.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104)

[![Image 397: Devastation of a tornado that passed through a rural field](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/2011_Lake_Martin_EF2_damage_Alabama_State_Route_9.png/250px-2011_Lake_Martin_EF2_damage_Alabama_State_Route_9.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2011_Lake_Martin_EF2_damage_Alabama_State_Route_9.png)

EF2 damage to trees located off [AL 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_State_Route_9 "Alabama State Route 9") northeast of Dexter.

The tornado first touched down north of [Wetumpka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wetumpka,_Alabama "Wetumpka, Alabama") in [Elmore County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elmore_County,_Alabama "Elmore County, Alabama"),[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-173) south of Charity Lane at approximately 8:12 p.m. CDT (01:12 UTC). It began to track just east of due north along Grier Road (CR 209) at high-end EF1 intensity, snapping trees and blowing out the south facing gable-end of the roof of a home.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Damage_Viewer-113)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BMXsum-174)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Elmoresum-175) The tornado then turned northeastward, continuing to snap and uproot trees as it moved through generally unpopulated, rural areas.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) The tornado then intensified to high-end EF2 intensity with winds of 130 mph (210 km/h) as it passed through the northwest side of [Dexter](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dexter,_Alabama&action=edit&redlink=1 "Dexter, Alabama (page does not exist)"), heavily damaging several homes. One home had its roof removed and a section of an exterior wall knocked down and a mobile home was rolled and obliterated with the debris blown several hundred yards. The residents of the mobile home had seen the tornado warning issued on their TV and went to a neighbor's house for safety before the tornado struck. There was major damage to farm equipment and outbuildings in this area as well.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BMXsum-174)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Elmoresum-175) The tornado continued northeastward through forested areas, continuing to cause EF2 damage. A home along Powell Road had its roof removed and multiple exterior walls knocked down. Eight people in the home received the warning and took shelter in a hallway before the tornado struck; only one of them was injured. Three barns and several outbuildings and tractors on the property were completely destroyed as well.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) The tornado then tracked over neighborhoods along [SR 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_State_Route_9 "Alabama State Route 9"), damaging several homes, and debarking and snapping trees.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BMXsum-174)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Elmoresum-175) Another mobile home in this area was rolled and disintegrated with the appliances found 400 yards (370 m) away. The occupants heard warning and sought shelter in the basement of a home across the road before.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) The tornado then passed south of [Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Central,_Elmore_County,_Alabama&action=edit&redlink=1 "Central, Elmore County, Alabama (page does not exist)"), continuing to cause EF2 damage in densely forested areas.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104)

The tornado then intensified to EF3 strength as it reached Central Road (CR 418). A mobile home along the road was completely destroyed; its two occupants heard the warning, but were unable to get to safe shelter, resulting in them being trapped and seriously injured in the debris of the home. Northeast of there along Old Colley Road (CR 417), several homes had their roofs blown off with one home having exterior walls knocked down.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) The tornado then crossed the Middle Road and Auction Barn Road intersection and struck a mobile home park, destroying 10 mobile homes and killing four people.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BMXsum-174)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Elmoresum-175) A home in the park was struck by the debris from the mobile homes and the exterior and the interior walls in the middle of the home were knocked down.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) The tornado then weakened to EF2 intensity as it continued to track northeastward through densely forested areas and passed just narrowly south of the town of [Falkner](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Falkner,_Alabama&action=edit&redlink=1 "Falkner, Alabama (page does not exist)"), causing mainly tree damage, although one home along Union Road suffered heavy roof and exterior wall damage.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) The tornado then strengthened to EF3 intensity again as it moved along Mount Hebron Road (CR 80) east of Falkner.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) Several homes, businesses, including the W W Monument Company, two churches, and an agricultural nursery were completely destroyed in this area.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BMXsum-174)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Elmoresum-175) One of the churches (Mount Baptist Church) had sanctuary debris blown 100–200 yards (91–183 m), the second-story of a split level home was removed, and a home along Nero Rock Road was unroofed and had two exterior walls knocked down.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) The tornado then weakened back to EF2 intensity and passed just north of [Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jordan,_Alabama&action=edit&redlink=1 "Jordan, Alabama (page does not exist)"), narrowly missing it.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) As it approached [Lake Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Martin "Lake Martin"), the tornado uprooted and snapped numerous trees.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) The tornado then crossed over [SR 63](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_State_Route_63 "Alabama State Route 63") and tracked into the Lake Martin area, maintaining EF2 strength as it crossed over the lake south of the SR 63 bridge. After moving ashore, the tornado regained EF3 intensity as it grew to its peak width of 0.5 miles (0.80 km) and reached [Windermere](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Windermere,_Alabama&action=edit&redlink=1 "Windermere, Alabama (page does not exist)").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Elmoresum-175) Numerous trees were snapped and partially debarked, thin electrical transmission towers were crumbled, and numerous homes suffered significant damage.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BMXsum-174)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Elmoresum-175)

[![Image 398: Scene of widespread destruction, with damaged vehicles and debris strewn across the landscape after a hurricane](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Lake_Martin_tornado_Mountain_View_Way_damage.png/250px-Lake_Martin_tornado_Mountain_View_Way_damage.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lake_Martin_tornado_Mountain_View_Way_damage.png)

EF4 damage to lakeside homes and boats on Mountain View Way

[![Image 399: A destroyed house and landscape is shown after a tornado](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/2011_Lake_Martin_tornado_historic_home_damage_EF3.png/250px-2011_Lake_Martin_tornado_historic_home_damage_EF3.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2011_Lake_Martin_tornado_historic_home_damage_EF3.png)

EF3 damage to a 100-year-old home located on County Road 54

The tornado then tracked back into Lake Martin and crossed in [Tallapoosa County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallapoosa_County,_Alabama "Tallapoosa County, Alabama") while retaining EF3 intensity.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) The tornado then became violent, reaching low-end EF4 strength with winds up to 170 mph (270 km/h) as it moved ashore on Stoney Ridge Road.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Tallapoosasum-176) Several well-built multi-story homes were leveled with no walls left standing above the basement level.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BMXsum-174)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Tallapoosasum-176) This included a two-story home located on the northern portion of Sandy Lane that was leveled with debris from the structure thrown into the lake.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) Four lakeside homes located off Mountain View Way were also leveled.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) Continuing northeastward, the tornado narrowed to 400 yards (370 m), but remained at low-end EF4 intensity as it crossed [SR 49](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_State_Route_49 "Alabama State Route 49"), destroying two homes.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BMXsum-174)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Tallapoosasum-176) One of the homes was a wood-frame house on a CMU stack column pier foundation; this home was completely obliterated and a [Ford F-150](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_F-Series "Ford F-Series") pickup truck that was parked in the driveway was thrown over 150–200 yards (140–180 m) and mangled. Trees were also debarked in the area of the slabbed residence.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) The tornado then weakened to EF3 intensity as it continued northeastward and tracked through forested areas before moving into the southeastern part of [Dadeville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadeville,_Alabama "Dadeville, Alabama").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) The tornado then crossed [US 280](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_280 "U.S. Route 280") on the east side of town, significantly damaging several homes and businesses. An elderly woman was killed in one of the homes and winds in this area were estimated to be up to 155 mph (249 km/h).[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BMXsum-174)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Tallapoosasum-176) The tornado continued northeastward through forested areas, before crossing into [Chambers County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chambers_County,_Alabama "Chambers County, Alabama").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104)

The tornado remained at EF3 intensity as it moved into Chambers County and continued its northeastward heading.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104) Along County Road 54, a 100-year-old wood-framed home on a brick column pier raised foundation was completely obliterated; winds in this area were estimated to be up to 150 mph (240 km/h).[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BMXsum-174) The tornado then gradually weakened as it continued northeastward through densely forested areas. Trees were snapped or uprooted along this final portion of the path before the tornado dissipated at 9:09 p.m. CDT (02:09 UTC) after tracking 44.18 miles (71.10 km) and reaching a maximum width of 880 yards (800 m).[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-BMXsum-174)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Elmoresum-175)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Tallapoosasum-176)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:1-103) Pilot Charles Moon surveyed the path and drew out an area of "total destruction".[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-178) Losses totaled $167 million (2011 USD). Seven people were killed by the tornado, and 30 others were injured.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:12-179)

This wide, EF3-rated tornado touched down at 12:38 a.m. on [U.S. Route 19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_19 "U.S. Route 19"), moving to the northeast. It maintained EF0 intensity as it tracked over relatively unpopulated areas, including the Three Mile Creek and Hay Road. The tornado reached EF1 intensity for the first time east of [Vega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega,_Georgia "Vega, Georgia"), while gradually widening. It abruptly began producing EF3-rated damage as its outer circulation impacted the Milner Crossroads area near [Piedmont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piedmont,_Georgia "Piedmont, Georgia"). Heavy damage was inflicted to a home north of [Barnesville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnesville,_Georgia "Barnesville, Georgia"), where the tornado would weaken to EF2 intensity. The tornado produced EF2 damage to a gas station and another building as it passed over Atlanta Street. It maintained EF1 intensity as it gradually thinned out north of the Hog Mountain. It began to widen as it strengthened in relatively unpopulated areas south of [Unionville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unionville,_Georgia "Unionville, Georgia"). EF2 damage was inflicted to softwood trees off of Wise Road. It continued producing EF2 damage before lifting southeast of [Blount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blount,_Georgia "Blount, Georgia") at 1:17 a.m. on April 28.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:0-104)

### Flooding (April 25–28)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Flooding (April 25–28)")]

[![Image 400: Weather map showing precipitation in the continental United States on April 25, 2011](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Pcpnweekending04292011.jpg/250px-Pcpnweekending04292011.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pcpnweekending04292011.jpg)

Rainfall totals within the United States for the week ending during the morning of April 29, 2011, which shows the extent of the heavy rain event this cyclone contributed towards.

This storm system prolonged an ongoing heavy rain event, which began across Arkansas and Missouri on April 22.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-SS11-23) Weekly rainfall totals reached 19.73 inches (501 mm) 6 miles (9.7 km) east-northeast of [Springdale, Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springdale,_Arkansas "Springdale, Arkansas"), 16.20 inches (411 mm) 4 miles (6.4 km) northwest of [Poplar Bluff, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poplar_Bluff,_Missouri "Poplar Bluff, Missouri"), and 14.96 inches (380 mm) at [Westville, Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westville,_Oklahoma "Westville, Oklahoma").[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-180) On April 25, 2011, thunderstorms with high winds swept through parts of southern and southeastern Ohio. Straight-line winds estimated at 80 miles per hour (130 km/h) uprooted trees, damaged roofs, and downed power lines through [Perry County, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perry_County,_Ohio "Perry County, Ohio"), and [Athens County, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens_County,_Ohio "Athens County, Ohio"). Strong thunderstorms and heavy downpours which led to flooding were also reported in areas across Upstate New York with heavy flooding in the [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse,_New_York "Syracuse, New York") area. The rain also saturated hundreds of lakes in the [Adirondack mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adirondack_mountains "Adirondack mountains"). [Interstate 81](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_81 "Interstate 81") was briefly shut down in the downtown area at traffic hour and the [State University of New York Upstate Medical University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_University_of_New_York_Upstate_Medical_University "State University of New York Upstate Medical University") also closed briefly due to flooding in the lobby.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-181) Heavy rains combined with rapid snowmelt caused widespread flooding across [Vermont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermont "Vermont") on April 26–27. Over the two-day period, up to 5 inches (130 mm) of rain fell across the northern third of Vermont, and up to 3 inches (76 mm) elsewhere across the state and extending into western [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts"). Numerous roads were closed across Vermont due to flooding, with some roads being completely washed out.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-182)

Farther south, flash flooding late on April 26 resulted in two fatalities in [Monroe, Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monroe,_Louisiana "Monroe, Louisiana"), after an apartment complex was swamped. The flooding there was considered to be worse than the flooding after [Hurricane Gustav](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Gustav "Hurricane Gustav") in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Atlantic_hurricane_season "2008 Atlantic hurricane season").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Shreveport-042611-41) In central and northern Arkansas, up to 10.44 inches (265 mm) of rain was reported during that week. The resulting flash flooding in central Arkansas also resulted in five people losing their lives. Many roads were closed due to the flooding there. The flooding was mitigated somewhat by a significant [drought](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drought "Drought") that had existed before the storm.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-NWSLittleRockApril27-83)

Severe thunderstorms were reported as far north as [Northern Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ontario "Northern Ontario") on the evening of April 26. Heavy rains and minor flooding were also reported in Northern Ontario from April 26–28.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-183)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-184)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-185)[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-186) Windstorms were also reported in [Southern Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Ontario "Southern Ontario") and Southern [Quebec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec "Quebec") which resulted in several injuries and one death, damages and power outages.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-ottawacitizen.com-187)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-theweathernetwork.com-188)[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Fierce_winds_whip_through_Ontario-189)[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-JMontreal-190)[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Zone-911-191)

Other fatalities due to straight-line winds occurred early on April 26 in [McComb, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McComb,_Mississippi "McComb, Mississippi")[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Apr25SPC-29) and early on April 27 in [Moody, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moody,_Alabama "Moody, Alabama"), [Vestavia Hills, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vestavia_Hills,_Alabama "Vestavia Hills, Alabama"), and [Franklin, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin,_Tennessee "Franklin, Tennessee"), from the squall line with embedded tornadoes.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Storm_Reports_April_27-20)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Storm_Reports_April_26-39)

Although the exact number of people killed during the outbreak is a source of debate, the generally accepted number is in the 300–350 range.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-192) 271 of those deaths occurred on April 27, the date of peak activity.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:1-103)[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-193)

The high number of fatalities on April 27 was studied in detail following the event. Despite 92 tornado warnings being issued for Alabama,[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-194) 271 people were killed, many in poorly built homes.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:1-103) In a study of people killed during the outbreak published by the [American Journal of Public Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Journal_of_Public_Health "American Journal of Public Health"), it was determined that only 102, or 41.3%, out of the 247 victims studied received a warning.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-195): e5–e6  It was determined that the majority of fatalities during the outbreak happened because of a lack of adequate community shelters in rural communities throughout Alabama.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-196)

### Immediate recovery efforts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Immediate recovery efforts")]

Alabama Governor [Robert J. Bentley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_J._Bentley "Robert J. Bentley") declared a state of emergency in the state of Alabama on April 27, due to storm damage from severe thunderstorms earlier that day as well as forthcoming severe weather later that day. States of emergency were also declared in Arkansas, [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky"), Mississippi, Missouri, [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee"), and Oklahoma because of the flooding and tornadoes.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-197) Following the tornado outbreak on the evening of April 27, [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")[Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") granted a federal emergency declaration for the state of Alabama, giving federal assistance, including search and rescue assets, to the affected region.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-198)

More than 2,000 [National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Guard_of_the_United_States "National Guard of the United States") troops were deployed to Alabama, assisting local and state first responders in search and rescue efforts.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-199) President Obama visited the affected areas of Alabama on April 29.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-200) Also on April 29, he approved a federal disaster declaration for seven Mississippi counties: [Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarke_County,_Mississippi "Clarke County, Mississippi"), [Greene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greene_County,_Mississippi "Greene County, Mississippi"), [Hinds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinds_County,_Mississippi "Hinds County, Mississippi"), [Jasper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasper_County,_Mississippi "Jasper County, Mississippi"), [Kemper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kemper_County,_Mississippi "Kemper County, Mississippi"), [Lafayette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lafayette_County,_Mississippi "Lafayette County, Mississippi"), and [Monroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monroe_County,_Mississippi "Monroe County, Mississippi").[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-201)

Storms through the area severely damaged [Tennessee Valley Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Valley_Authority "Tennessee Valley Authority") (TVA)'s [power grid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_power_transmission "Electric power transmission") for transmitting electricity throughout the region. More than 300 power transmission towers, 120 to 150 feet (37 to 46 m) tall, were destroyed in the storms, some "twisted like bow ties" according to National Weather Service meteorologist Eric Holweg. The towers supported some 90 transmission lines, a mixture of 500[kV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volt "Volt") and 161kV lines. Those lines provided power from TVA to 128 regional distributors.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-202)[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-bowTieTower-203)

[![Image 406: An electrical tower is bent in an arched shape against a blue sky](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Electric_line_tower.jpg/250px-Electric_line_tower.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Electric_line_tower.jpg)

Transmission tower bent near [Huntsville, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntsville,_Alabama "Huntsville, Alabama").

TVA lost the ability to transmit power from both [Browns Ferry Nuclear Power Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Browns_Ferry_Nuclear_Power_Plant "Browns Ferry Nuclear Power Plant") and [Widows Creek Fossil Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Widows_Creek_Power_Plant "Widows Creek Power Plant") after the storms on April 27, requiring both to be shut down. The nuclear plant's [cold shutdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shutdown_(nuclear_reactor) "Shutdown (nuclear reactor)") was supported by diesel generators for four days until a second 161kV line could be restored to the plant. The loss of redundant off-site power required a "notification of unusual event", the lowest of four levels of concern dictated by the [NRC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_Regulatory_Commission "Nuclear Regulatory Commission"). Some 60 percent of the sirens for warning residents of worse problems around Browns Ferry were disabled by the storms, and the plant had to arrange plans to use cars with loudspeakers to warn residents in case of another problem.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-TFP-nuke-110)[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-bowTieTower-203) The Nuclear Regulatory Commission stated at a press conference: "The plants' conditions are stable and are being placed in a cooled-down condition."[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-UPI-nuke-204)[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-205)

[Huntsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntsville,_Alabama "Huntsville, Alabama") was the largest city with no electricity from TVA.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-bowTieTower-203) All the traffic lights were off, a dusk-to-dawn curfew was imposed, students were sent home from [United States Space Camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Space_Camp "United States Space Camp"), and the [Panoply Arts Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panoply_Arts_Festival "Panoply Arts Festival") was canceled.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-206)[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-207)[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-208) Power was restored gradually to Huntsville, beginning with 3 percent on the morning of May 1.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-3percent-209) Only localized outages remained eight days after the storm.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-210) In addition to traffic and safety issues, the outage caused difficulties with water treatment and distribution and retail of all kinds, including [gasoline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gasoline "Gasoline") and food purchases.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-3percent-209)[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-211)

Ontario electricity outages were minor, mostly caused by the windstorms of April 28. Although they affected thousands of people at different times throughout the day, all power was restored by the end of the day.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-ottawacitizen.com-187)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-theweathernetwork.com-188)[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Fierce_winds_whip_through_Ontario-189)[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-JMontreal-190)[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Zone-911-191)
